Moudud Ahmed with KS Hossain, Md. Munsur Ali and Sk. Rezaul Karim, Advocates  ------- For the Petitioner.

parties:
Hussain Mohammad Ershad ------- Petitioner. 
Vs. 
State  ------- Opposite Party
full_judgment: 12. Mr. Aminul Huq, the learned Attorney- General who opposed this application, submitted that this application is initially not maintainable for the reason that under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure a Court can postpone a trial or a proceeding if the court thinks fit at his discretion that there are reasonable grounds for doing so but in the instant case at the beginning of the trial an application of this nature had been moved and the court at that time rejected the application on detailed grounds stated therein but that order had not been challenged before this Court and there is nothing on record to show that any application had in fact been moved before any Division Bench is Revision for it to be withdrawn as claimed now and, according to the learned Attorney General, no such application had in fact been produced before the court for it to be withdrawn and for withdrawal of a petition after submission before the court which becomes a property of the court it needs permission of the court for such withdrawal which is not the case here. Therefore, the application moved now before this Court describing it to be a supplementary affidavit of the petition already moved in the month of May, 1991 and subsequently withdrawn is not at all correct. It is rather a clever device to bypass the law of limitation because a Revision under the practice of this Court is to be moved within a certain period after the passing of the impugned order which date has long lapsed and now totally barred by limitation and further this application now moved after the close of the defence case and the close of the arguments of both the parties cannot be contemplated to be an application under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure because an application under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure could be moved to postpone a "trial" but in the instant case the trial has come to an end. According to the learned Attorney-General, a judgment would not include a trial as such but a petition to postpone the trial needs to be moved before the trial is over, and in that the learned Attorney-General refers to certain decisions of Indian jurisdiction to which we shall advert at the relevant portion of the judgment. The learned Attorney-General further submitted that public policy demands that criminal case need be heard at the earliest possible time so that evidence for the prosecution is not lost in the process and in the instant case the criminal proceeding having beer. instituted not by a private individual but the State and having been instituted before the civil suit, which civil suit is termed by the Attorney-General to be an afterthought the criminal proceeding need not be stayed and in reply to the argument of the learned Counsel Mr. Moudud Ahmed it is the submission of the Attorney-General that a civil case of this nature would definitely take time and therefore nobody could say when it would come to an end and the present criminal case would be hanging there for an indefinite period which cannot be done and this is the consistent view of the courts of this sub-continent in this regard. Mr. Attorney-General, by reference to certain facts and to the reasoning's of the court below in rejecting the criminal application under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, submitted to the effect that it is in evidence that the notes all of 500.00 denomination were found in "bundles" and those were found not in a wooden box or in a cash box or in an iron safe but in 25 steel trunks and the money amounting to Tk. 2.00 crores in cash were scattered found in those 25 trunks boxes under the clothes. These were folded therein and each of those bundles were tagged with a seal of a Bank and the names of the Banks were in those Bank seals and the seals were of the Bangladesh Bank, Janata Bank, Al-Baraka Bank and other banks and those notes in bundles were prima facie withdrawn from those Banks and referring to the deposition of Tajul Islam DW 1 who, according to the learned Attorney-General, is the key witness for the defence and who according to all the defence witnesses had been in charge of collecting of the money from the members of the Jatiya Party for the purpose of purchasing a house of the Jatiya Party at Dhanmondi Residential Area Dhaka, who deposed in court that from the month of August, 1990, he did not withdraw money from the Bank, the learned Attorney General submits that if that be the position then this money is definitely not Jatiya Party money because the Bank seal clearly shows those were withdrawn from the Banks on 18.8.90, 18.8.90, 3.8.90, 3.8.90, 25.7.90 and so on and on this ground the learned Attorney-General submits that the money referred to in that Money Suit cannot be the money of Jatiya Party collected from donation of hundreds of its members found in the possession which possession, according to the learned Attorney-General, is accepted by the accused at the trial but only defending that it is party money. Thus postponement of the criminal case, for the money suit to be disposed of earlier would be unwarranted because prima facie that money directly came from Bank with Bank seal intact in all those bundles and those are not laboriously collected money from the Party members. According to the learned Attorney- General this money had been given to the accused by others, may be in different installments, directly withdrawing the cash in bundles from the Bank and this huge amount of money is illegal earning of the accused and this recovered money with Bank seals in bundles is and cannot be the money substantially at issue in both the Criminal and the Money Suit filed by a third party. The learned Attorney-General further submits that this exercise of power under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is discretion of the court and that discretion of the court was exercised with cogent reason. This High Court in exercise of its revisional power should not interfere with such discretion as a matter of course if the order rejecting the application was not perverse or totally without jurisdiction or totally unwarranted causing failure of justice and, according to the learned Attorney-General, the rejection of the application under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure initially was with cogent reasons for it has been clearly mentioned in that order rejecting the application under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure that these is no fixity of title in cash money which means that it became the money of that person to whom it goes in due course, if not specifically proved otherwise. The other reasons of the court below in rejecting the application was that in that suit the claim by Jatiya Party is against the accused and if the suit is decreed it is the accused who should be responsible and account for it and for that and at the request of the accused of the criminal trial the money suit cannot be postponed.
